title: Simulation of Half-Wave Rectifier in MATLAB/Simulink
aim: To simulate a Half-Wave Rectifier circuit with and without a shunt capacitor filter and observe the rectified pulsating DC output waveform.
apparatus_components: AC Sinusoidal Voltage Source V1 (Vm = 10 V peak, f = 50 Hz, Node 1 to GND)
Rectifier Diode D1 (1N4007, Anode at Node 1, Cathode at Node 2)
Load Resistor R1 = 1 kΩ (Node 2 to GND)
Optional Shunt Filter Capacitor C1 = 100 µF (Node 2 to GND)
theory: A Half-Wave Rectifier converts alternating current (AC) into unidirectional pulsating DC using a single PN-junction diode. During the positive half-cycle (V_in > 0.7 V), D1 is forward-biased and conducts current to load resistor R1, producing V_out_peak = V_m - 0.7 V. During the negative half-cycle, D1 is reverse-biased (blocking) and V_out = 0 V. Adding a shunt filter capacitor C1 in parallel with R1 smooths the output by charging to V_out_peak and discharging slowly with time constant R1*C1 during the non-conducting interval.
equations: Peak Rectified Load Voltage: V_peak_out = V_m - 0.7 V
Average (DC) Output Voltage (unfiltered): V_dc = V_peak_out / pi ≈ 0.318 * V_peak_out
Ripple Factor (unfiltered): gamma = 1.21; (with filter C): gamma ≈ 1 / (2 * sqrt(3) * f * R1 * C1)
circuit_topology: AC source V1 (N1 -> GND) feeding series diode D1 (N1 -> N2) and load resistor R1 (N2 -> GND), with optional filter capacitor C1 across R1.
component_relationships: V1: N1 -> GND (AC Sine Source, 10 V peak, 50 Hz)
R1: N2 -> GND (1 kΩ load resistor)
C1 (optional): N2 -> GND (Shunt filter capacitor in parallel with R1)
simulation_type: Transient Analysis over 2–3 AC cycles (40 ms at 50 Hz)
procedure:
1. Connect AC sinusoidal voltage source V1 (10 V peak, 50 Hz) between Node 1 and GND.
2. Connect diode D1 from Node 1 to Node 2 and load resistor R1 (1 kΩ) from Node 2 to GND.
3. Run transient simulation for 40 ms and plot both input AC voltage V(1) and rectified output voltage V(2).
4. Optionally connect filter capacitor C1 across R1 to observe ripple smoothing.
expected_observations: Positive half-cycles appear at Node 2 with peak 9.3 V (10 V - 0.7 V), while negative half-cycles are clipped to 0 V.
result: The Half-Wave Rectifier was simulated and its input/output waveforms were verified.
common_mistakes: Using a DC source instead of a sinusoidal source when trying to plot rectified waveforms
Connecting the filter capacitor in series with the load instead of in parallel across the load

viva_concepts.a: Rectification is the conversion of bidirectional alternating current (AC) into unidirectional pulsating direct current (DC).

viva_concepts.q: Why is the efficiency of a half-wave rectifier limited to 40.6%?
viva_concepts.a: Because the entire negative half-cycle of the AC input wave is blocked and wasted, and power is only delivered during the positive half-cycle.

viva_concepts.q: How does a capacitor connected across the load reduce ripple in a half-wave rectifier?
viva_concepts.a: The capacitor charges to V_peak during the positive peak and discharges slowly through the load resistor R1 with time constant R1*C1 when the diode is off, keeping V_out near V_peak.

viva_concepts.q: What is the Peak Inverse Voltage (PIV) rating required for the diode in a half-wave rectifier?
viva_concepts.a: Without filter, PIV = V_m. With a capacitor filter, PIV = 2 * V_m because the cathode stays charged near +V_m while the anode swings to -V_m.

viva_concepts.q: What is the output ripple frequency of a half-wave rectifier driven by a 50 Hz AC supply?
viva_concepts.a: 50 Hz (equal to the input AC frequency f), because there is one output pulse per full AC cycle.

viva_concepts.q: How do you declare a 10 V, 50 Hz sinusoidal source in PySpice?
How is the filter capacitor C1 connected relative to the load resistor R1?
viva_concepts.a: In parallel (across) the load resistor R1, between Node 2 and GND.

viva_concepts.q: For a 15 V peak AC input and a silicon diode (0.7 V drop), what are V_peak_out and V_dc (unfiltered)?
What happens to the output waveform if diode D1 is reversed in a half-wave rectifier?
viva_concepts.a: The positive half-cycles are blocked and the negative half-cycles pass through, producing a negative half-wave rectified output.

viva_concepts.q: What happens to the ripple voltage if the filter capacitance C1 is increased?
viva_concepts.a: The time constant R1*C1 increases, so the capacitor discharges less between peaks and the peak-to-peak ripple voltage decreases.

EXPERIMENT-14

Date:

SIMULATION OF FULLWAVE RECTIFIER IN MATLAB/SIMULINK
Aim: To simulate the operation of full-wave rectifier with and without filter circuits in
MATLAB/Simulink and analyse their output waveforms.
Apparatus Required:
•

MATLAB/Simulink software installed on a computer.

•

Diode – for rectification.

•

AC Voltage Source – to supply the input signal.

•

Resistive Load (R) – to represent the load for the rectifier.

•

Capacitor (optional) – for filtering the output (to smooth the ripple).

•

Scope block – to observe the waveforms.

•

Voltage Measurement Blocks – to measure input and output voltages.

•

Current Measurement Blocks – to measure load current.

•

Power GUI block – for simulation control.
Circuit Diagram

Procedure:
1. Simulation of Full-Wave Rectifier (Without Filter):
Step 1: Create a new Simulink model for the Full-Wave Rectifier (Bridge Configuration).
Step 2: Drag and drop the following components:

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import PySpice.Logging.Logging as Logging
logger = Logging.setup_logging()
from PySpice.Spice.Netlist import Circuit
from PySpice.Unit import *

# Topology Classification: EXACT MANUAL TOPOLOGY
circuit = Circuit('Half-Wave Rectifier (Experiment 13)')
circuit.model('1N4007', 'D', IS=7.027e-9@u_A, RS=0.034@u_Ohm, N=1.77, BV=1000@u_V)
circuit.SinusoidalVoltageSource(1, 1, circuit.gnd, amplitude=12@u_V, frequency=50@u_Hz)
circuit.Diode(1, 1, 2, model='1N4007')
circuit.R(1, 2, circuit.gnd, 1@u_kOhm)

# 1. Run the transient simulation
simulator = circuit.simulator(temperature=25, nominal_temperature=25)
analysis = simulator.transient(step_time=100@u_us, end_time=60@u_ms)

# 2. Extract input and rectified output voltage waveforms
time_axis = np.array(analysis.time)
v_output = np.array(analysis['2'])
v_input = np.array(analysis['1'])
i_load = v_output / float(circuit.R1.resistance)

# 3. Create the waveform plot and 4. Label axes appropriately
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(time_axis, v_input, '--', color='gray', label='AC Input Voltage V(1)')
plt.plot(time_axis, v_output, color='black', linewidth=2, label='Rectified Output Voltage V(2)')
plt.title('Half-Wave Rectifier (Experiment 13): Input vs Rectified Output Waveform')
plt.xlabel('Time [s]')
plt.ylabel('Voltage [V]')
plt.grid(True)
plt.legend(loc='upper right')

# 5. Save and display the result
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('rectifier_waveform.png', dpi=150)
plt.show()
